records.finding: advanceBodies reads source positions from bodies into shared-memory tiles, then writes updated positions back to the same global bodies array in that kernel. __syncthreads only synchronizes a block; there is no grid-wide barrier between all reads and any writes. Different blocks can therefore consume a mixture of old and updated positions. This is a pre-existing cross-block race, not a timing issue or a floating-point hash mismatch.
records.observed_failure: At 1031 bodies and 11 steps, execution and internal validation pass but the unchanged numerical comparator rejects the sum: reference 6.0677587880213544 versus 5.1882088020953523. Min/max and several printed samples also differ substantially.
records.interpretation: The nonmultiple body count introduces a partially active fifth 256-thread block. The source race is unconditional; the observed numerical discrepancy is consistent with changed block scheduling. No claim is made that this is the only triggering input.

records.finding: computeFormFactors creates a distinct MT19937 stream for each receiver row, seeded with 42 + 0x9e3779b9 * i. The unchanged input uses one stream seeded with 42 across the entire ordered pair traversal. This changes the sampled form factors. The changed random stream is consistent with the final-distance discrepancy; it has not been isolated as the sole numerical cause.
records.observed_failure: At -n 320 -t 101 -s 7 -r 0.7, execution and internal validation pass. The distance sum is 4703 rather than the reference 4772.5: an absolute error of 69.5, exceeding the existing Roomsim sum tolerance of 50. The disposition follows this numerical failure, not a hash mismatch or the changed sampling strategy alone.
records.timing_correction_check: The original-to-corrected source diff only changes the total elapsed duration to a maximum-rank interval. It does not change form-factor streams or numerical computation.
